newsOverlay.marketBias: Oil has fallen for a third session as Saudi supply-disruption fears ease, reducing part of the immediate inflation shock, while the Fed/BOJ tightening backdrop remains restrictive. WATCH only; this does not create a buy signal.

items.headline: Oil falls for third session as Saudi supply-disruption fears ease
items.summary: Reuters reports Brent fell about 2% to $102.68 and WTI to $100.08 as Saudi pipeline capacity restoration and alternative loadings reduced immediate supply fears. Lower oil pressure eases part of the inflation/liquidity shock, though geopolitical and monetary-policy risks remain.
items.whyItMatters: Energy prices are a key transmission channel into inflation expectations, yields and risk-asset liquidity; a sustained oil retreat can reduce near-term macro pressure on crypto.
items.actionReason: Material macro reversal/extension, but positive relief never creates a buy signal.

items.headline: Ueda gives cautious guidance after BOJ hike; yen weakens as immediate event risk resolves
items.summary: Reuters reports Ueda stressed data-dependent policy, risks from energy costs and financial stability, without strong guidance on the timing of another hike. The yen weakened and Asian stocks rose, indicating the immediate market read was less hawkish than feared.
items.whyItMatters: The scheduled BOJ communication risk has passed without a clearly more-hawkish surprise; this reduces immediate event risk but global monetary tightening remains a headwind.
items.actionReason: Major HIGH catalyst resolution. Positive market reaction does not create a buy signal.

items.headline: BOJ raises policy rate to 1.25%, 31-year high
items.summary: Reuters confirms the BOJ raised its policy rate from 1.00% to 1.25% in a 7-2 vote; the yen weakened after the widely expected decision.
items.whyItMatters: Japanese tightening can affect yen carry trades, global yields and risk-asset liquidity.
items.actionReason: The rate decision and press conference are now resolved; no independent buy or sell instruction.

items.headline: Goldman Sachs shifts to October Fed hike call as markets price further tightening
items.summary: Reuters reports Goldman Sachs now expects another 25 bp Fed hike in October after the September increase; traders price meaningful additional tightening risk.
items.whyItMatters: A higher expected Fed path can pressure risk-asset liquidity and crypto valuations.
items.actionReason: Material macro repricing is a risk input, not an independent sell instruction.

items.headline: SEC grants five-year conditional exemption for tokenized U.S. stock trading
items.summary: Reuters reports the SEC introduced a five-year exemption allowing qualifying platforms to trade tokenized stocks with full shareholder rights, while synthetic derivative tokens remain prohibited.
items.whyItMatters: The exemption expands regulated U.S. use of blockchain market infrastructure.
items.actionReason: Positive regulatory news never creates a buy signal.

items.headline: Dollar eases from seven-week peak as oil extends decline after Fed hike
items.summary: Reuters reports the dollar retreated from its post-Fed seven-week high while oil extended declines.
items.whyItMatters: A softer dollar and lower oil can relieve part of the immediate tightening impulse for crypto.
items.actionReason: Material reversal, not a buy signal.

items.headline: Bitcoin and Ether spot ETF outflows extend to a second session after Fed hike
items.summary: Public reporting citing finalized Farside data says U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs lost about $295.9M and spot Ether ETFs $224.1M on September 16.
items.whyItMatters: A second consecutive large redemption session indicates material near-term institutional flow pressure.
items.actionReason: Material flow pressure, not an independent sell instruction.

items.headline: Hawkish Fed lifts dollar to seven-week high as markets reprice tightening path
items.summary: Reuters reports the dollar index reached its strongest level since July 31 as short-term U.S. yields rose after the Fed hike.
items.whyItMatters: A stronger dollar and higher front-end yields transmit tighter Fed policy into less favorable crypto liquidity.

items.headline: Warsh says inflation remains too high and underlying trends have not meaningfully improved
items.summary: Reuters reports Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said inflation remains too high and persistent.
items.whyItMatters: Hawkish guidance supports further tightening risk.
items.actionReason: Confirmed hawkish guidance remains context, not an independent sell instruction.

items.headline: Federal Reserve raises target rate 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00%
items.summary: Reuters confirms the Federal Reserve raised its key interest rate by 25 basis points and indicated more tightening is likely.
items.whyItMatters: Renewed Fed tightening can lift real yields and reduce risk-asset liquidity.
items.actionReason: Further tightening remains possible; not an independent sell instruction.
